correctness.rationale: For any rooted subtree the three states A (root selected), B (root omitted but child-selected domination), and C (root omitted and waiting for external parent) form an exact exhaustive partition. The displayed child-combination recurrences prove by simultaneous induction the strict cost gaps and all minimizing state counts for each height residue. The global root cannot take C, giving the exact level-set classification and formulas, including the h=0 and h=1 boundaries. Independently implemented enumeration verifies every minimum subset for 313 small-tree instances; a separate dynamic program verifies all 363 degree profiles through height 5 and 425 irregular instances through height 6 (1,101 instances total). Infinite scope comes from induction, not these finite checks.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 result identifies surprisingly bounded multiplicity for complete binary trees. The new finding proves the stronger, degree-profile invariant fact for *every* full-depth rooted tree with at least two children at every internal node, even with arbitrary vertex-level irregularity; all optimum sets are exactly classified. It provides closed formulas for the minimum and the entire minimizing family without running the general DP. The root-only alternative (one root or one root child) at heights divisible by three is a meaningful rigidity mechanism and informs solution diversity in hierarchical monitoring placements. It is not merely a renamed fixed-arity specialization.
